Hi Kevin,
You are correct. The construction of the
section of dual 300 mm watermain on Erbsville Road is required as part of the
Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive Project to support the proposed Beaver Creek Meadows residential
development.
Construction for the project is proposed to commence wit
h the works along Beaver Creek Road in 2018 at the earliest
pending approvals and property acquisition. The construction of dual watermain on Conservation Drive and Erbsville
Road likely won’t start until 2019 / 2020.
The budget for this project is curren
tly under review as part of the overall DC review at the City. Kevin what is the
Region’s current budget for this watermain? I would like to touch base with your to coordinate the budget for the dual
watermain portion of the works.
Let me know if you have
any questions.
Thanks,
Caroline

Hi Milos,
Regarding the proposed watermain on Erbsville Road, I understand that this watermain in included in the scope of work
that the City is undertaking with Stantec for th
e Beaver Creek / Conservation Drive reconstruction project. The Region has
money assigned for our share of the 300mm loop on Erbsville, Conservation, and Beaver Creek Road (it is a dual
ownership watermain) in 2017.

2
With regards to the Erbsville Road wat
ermain that will connect the Zone 5 loop, that section of road is up for a rural
resurfacing in 2024. So in order to implement the recommended pressure zone looping associated with the Beaver Creek
Meadows Plan, this watermain component would likely need t
o be conducted as a separate project outside of the
Region’s Transportation Capital Rural Resurfacing Program in advance of 2024, hence the inclusion in the City’s project.
Caroline, please advise if I am misinformed.

Hi Milos,
The Ministry of Natural Resources and Forestry (MNRF) Guelph District Office appreciates the opportunity to review the
City of Waterloo’s completed ‘Water Distribution Master Plan’ (WDMP).
It is understood that the WDMP has been
completed in accordance wi
th the Municipal Engineering Association (MEA) Master Plan Class Environmental
Assessment Process.
The WDMP (e.g. Section 4.4.3) describes that the Region of Waterloo plans to consolidate the Wat 4B, Wat 4C and Wat
5 pressure zones into the existing Wat 5
zone.
It is understood that this will require the construction of new
transmission watermains to merge the three pressure zones, as shown on Figure 3 (Regional Water System Upgrades) in
the WDMP.
Recently the MNRF reviewed and provided recommendations
to the City on the completed ‘Beaver Creek Road and
Conservation Drive Upgrades and Extension of Municipal Services’ Environmental Study Report (ESR).
The ESR
recommends the installation of watermains along Conservation Drive, Beaver Creek Road and Erbsv
ille Road.
I was
hoping the City could clarify if the new transmission watermains for Wat 5 are to be addressed during the City’s detailed
design work of the Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive servicing, or will this be a separate process?
Thanks
Dave
